meta.title: Marrow Key
meta.dek: Land at the north dock, walk through the keeper's house, wade into the salt marsh and find the hogs under the live oaks. Every animal you pick goes in your field journal.
byline: For visitors on the day ferry
Demonstration: Marrow Key, its keepers and every figure here are invented
meta.description: An illustrated field guide to an invented barrier island, with a map tour, a walk through a house, a marsh panorama with rigged animals and a tide, pen notes and a quiz played as golf.
meta.colophon:
Built by the chronicle plugin from a facts file and a story file. The drawings were made as SVG for this page and painted in ink and watercolor in code; the animals were drawn in parts and move about their joints.

Demonstration data. Marrow Key and everything on this page are invented for this example.

theme.concept: A naturalist's field notebook for a barrier island: ink sketches washed in marsh greens and sea blues, specimen labels, a tide table, a trail map with numbered stops.

map.alt: Watercolor map of Marrow Key: the salt marsh on the west side, live oak woods in the middle, the keeper's house on the rise and the north dock where the ferry lands.

dock.alt: The north dock at low water: the pier, the ferry tied up, a sign that reads No wake, and the high-water line on the pilings.

house-front.alt: The keeper's house from the lawn: pink stucco, a green door with a lamp beside it, oaks on either side.

house-hall.alt: The hall inside the keeper's house: paneled walls, a fireplace with a chart above it, a window to the marsh and the stair.

marsh.alt: A wide watercolor of Marrow Key from the salt marsh to the surf: cordgrass and a creek, the mudflat, the dunes and the beach.

woods.alt: A hog rooting under the live oaks, head down and tail going.

hero.caption: The north dock at low water. The ferry from Breton ties up here {{island.ferries_day}} a day.

blocks.text: Marrow Key is {{island.acres}} of marsh, woods and beach. The tour below walks the four places most visitors see in a day. Pick a stop on the map to open it, or read the chapters in order; the route in the bar at the top follows you either way.

blocks.text: The ferry takes {{island.ferry_minutes}} from Breton landing and ties up at the north dock. At low water the pilings show how high the tide came: the line is the mean high water, about {{marsh.tide_range}} above where you can see the mud now.

blocks.caption: Read the dock before you step off.

blocks.text: The house was finished in {{house.built|year}}, the year the light was lit, and {{house.keepers}} lived in it before the light ran itself. Walk in through the front door.

chapters.title: From the marsh to the surf

blocks.text: The tide comes in {{marsh.tides_day}} a day and covers the mudflat. Fiddler crabs feed on the flat at low water; dolphins come up the beach at high water. Drag the painting, pick the places along the top, and move the tide.

zones.label: Salt marsh
zones.text: Smooth cordgrass, flooded twice a day.

zones.label: Mudflat

notes.text: Low tide: the flat is bare and the crabs are out.
The tide is coming in over the flat.
High tide: the flat is under water and dolphins work the beach.

blocks.text: The hogs came with the first settlers and never left. They root under the oaks with their heads down and their tails going.

blocks.caption: Watch the snout and the tail.

questions.q: When are the fiddler crabs out on the flat?
questions.explain: They feed on the bare mud and go down their burrows when the tide covers it.

questions.q: What does the line on the pilings mark?
questions.explain: The line is where the tide reaches on an average day.

questions.q: Why is the keeper's house pink?
options: So the ferry could find it in fog
questions.explain: The keepers painted it so the ferry could pick it out from the channel.
